## What it is

The rules every person with system access reads and signs before access is granted, including social media and external site restrictions, with a register of acknowledgments, as SP 800-53 PL-4 requires.

## Preview (annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
PL-4 asks for rules that tell each person what they are responsible for and how they must behave when using the organization's information and systems, and for a signed acknowledgment before access is granted. Assessors sample new accounts and check that each has an acknowledgment dated before the account was created, and that people re-acknowledged after the rules last changed. Keep the rules short enough that people read them: link to the policies for detail. Add rules for privileged users, or keep a separate set for them.
:::

### Who these rules apply to

These rules apply to everyone who needs access to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>'s information or systems, including employees, contractors and partners. You must read and sign them before you are given access, and again <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; when the rules are revised or updated <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually, and when the rules are revised or updated</span></span> (PL-4b, PL-4d). Where re-acknowledgment is periodic, it is due <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency for individuals to read and re-acknowledge the rules of behavior <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span>.

### Your responsibilities

#### Accounts and passwords

- Use only the accounts issued to you, and only for the purposes they were issued for (AC-2).
- Keep your passwords, security keys and other authenticators to yourself. Never share them or write them where others can find them (IA-5).
- Lock your screen when you leave your device, and log off at the end of the day (AC-11).

#### Information

- Access only the information you need for your work (AC-6).
- Handle information according to its marking or sensitivity, and never remove it from approved systems without authorization (MP-4).
- Do not send organizational information to personal email, messaging or storage accounts.

#### Privacy

- Use personally identifiable information only for the purpose it was collected for, and only when your work requires it (PT-2).
- Share personally identifiable information only with people authorized to receive it.

#### Devices and software

- Use only devices the organization issued or approved to access its systems (AC-19).
- Do not install software, browser extensions or services that the organization has not approved (CM-11).
- Do not disable or bypass security software or settings.
- Report a lost or stolen device immediately.

#### Remote work

- Connect remotely only through the organization's approved remote access methods (AC-17).
- Do not let others use your device while you are connected to organizational systems.

#### Social media and external sites

- Do not use social media, social networking sites or other external sites and applications for organizational business unless <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: who approves such use, for example your manager and the communications team</span> has approved it (PL-4(1)(a)).
- Do not post organizational information on public websites unless it has been approved for public release (PL-4(1)(b)).
- Do not use your organizational email address or other organization-provided identifiers to create accounts on external sites or applications, except for approved business use (PL-4(1)(c)).
- Never use the password or other authentication secret for an organizational account on any external site or application (PL-4(1)(c)).

#### Monitoring

- <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> monitors the use of its systems, as the notice you see when you log on states (AC-8). Use of the systems means you agree to that monitoring.

#### Reporting

- Report a suspected security or privacy incident, including a phishing message you clicked, to <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: where to report, for example the service desk at a phone number or address</span> within <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: time to report, for example one hour</span> of noticing it (IR-6).

#### Consequences

- Breaking these rules may lead to loss of access and to action under the organization's sanctions process (PS-8).

### Acknowledgment

I have read these rules of behavior, I understand them, and I agree to follow them (PL-4b).

| Name | Title or role | Signature | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: name</span> | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: title or role</span> | | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: date</span> |

### Maintaining these rules

:::note[Guidance]
The acknowledgment must be recorded before access is authorized, so the account manager checks the register before creating the account (AC-2). Most organizations collect acknowledgments in the training or HR system; export the records into this register, or point to them, for the assessor.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall provide these rules to each person who requires access to the system, before access is requested. (PL-4a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall confirm that a signed acknowledgment is recorded before authorizing access. (PL-4b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review and update these rules <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency for reviewing and updating the rules of behavior <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span>. (PL-4c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall require each person who acknowledged a previous version to read and re-acknowledge the rules as the section "Who these rules apply to" states. (PL-4d)
